notes.text: This is a handwritten drawing sheet. Dark ink, lighter pencil strokes and two green strokes occur. The lighter heading and foliation are retained without assigning a named writer. No typescript is transcribed on this page.

The total visibly superposes 4 and 7. A 4 corrected to 7 remains favored, but the reverse order is explicit as an alternative. The listed quantities give 2+3+6+6=17, while the separately written parenthesis after deletion is 14=3×4+2. Both source expressions remain; arithmetic does not choose the overwrite order.

The whole right-hand note is crossed by three parallel oblique strokes and is now marked deleted. Its clear short form is un ens, followed by on fait 3×2=6. Avec, cartes and elliptiques remain doubtful under the cancellation. The final pair reads (1,1); its first 1 is dark and retraced, but no definite prior numeral is recoverable.

The type phrase is physically interlinear below trouver; its precise linear attachment remains uncertain. The cancelled glyph before the first J is separate from that J. Both live letters have a left-hooked foot and are read J.

The drawings remain schematic diplomatic reproductions. The independent second reading led to refinements in fifteen graphic boxes: open contours, doubled traces, separate arrowheads, rings and contact points. Correctly read first labels and both green strokes remain. Native coordinate scopes restore each drawing to its scan position, and overlapping neighbors and full-page lines are represented only once. The two large loop signs and crowded b/c labels remain doubtful.
No explicit date was read on this page. The handwritten 23 is retained as marginal foliation without assigning its hand.
The source forms ens and card are left unexpanded. No period is added after ens where H supplied one.

The cancelled right-hand note associates three elements with 3×2=6 elliptic cartes of type (1,1), with cartes and elliptiques themselves still doubtful. The sheet writes diag_Q ≃ omega_Q and diag_Q wedge omega_Q ≃ codiag_Q and enumerates canonical constructions from a four-element set. These are recorded as source claims; the only mathematical checks performed here remain the three elementary computations K24-01 through K24-03.

The main reader personally inspected all 32 differing boxes. Fifteen graphic traces, the cancelled margin note, the overwritten total and the word after it were revised; the overlapping bottom-text box was updated consistently. The preferred word is now ponts, with points retained because no secure i dot survives. The narrow arithmetic crop omits the leading 1, which is visible in the wide crop. No new mathematical proof or computation was performed during this audit.

main_review: Whole sheet and all 21 first-pass crops inspected; all open and changed places adjudicated. The written total remains doubtful; arithmetic is kept in the notes. Inventory and witness differences reviewed.

changes.ink: The inner loop is open and uneven, the central stem has two closely spaced traces, and several lower parts are separated by visible gaps. A short horizontal connection has a rightward head. The independent tracing retains these details more closely than the former regularized cup and stem. Two upper-right curves belong to the neighboring sphere and are not duplicated.

The outer boundary has an interruption near its upper-right end, with partial retracing at the top and lower-right. Three small directional marks and the broken interior paths are visible. Adopt those geometric details. The separate sign still has an outer loop, inner curl and small raised 3-like black mark; its identity remains circlearrowleft-with-3 versus script S_3, rather than treating the blind literal loops as a resolved sign.

The two outer contours have open gaps, and several small rings are themselves open or retraced. The lower-right narrow ring has a short descending leftward head. The independent paths preserve these irregular openings and retracings; the long line crossing the crop is retained once as a full-sheet connector.

On the clockwise-rotated crop the upper label is Q prime, the opposite lower label is Q, and the short middle label is ell double prime. These are not the blind bar-g, alpha and equals guesses from the unrotated crop. The clear d and circular-arrow label remain; b and c still merge with darker vertex strokes. The new geometry preserves the central polygon, internal triangles, paired arcs, small arrows and open contours. A letter-shaped ell stroke is not duplicated as a drawing curve.

The left and central outer contours are uneven and partly open, with distinct peripheral rings. The short stroke left of the central oval starts in blank space and has a visible rightward head. In the right sphere the upper-left rear connection is broken, but the lower-left connection is solid apart from the short separated arrow near its beginning. Both filled side-boundary points and the four rings remain. The second tracing is corrected at that lower connection; crossing full-sheet lines are not duplicated.

The arrow cluster has several distinct converging head strokes and partially separate oblique stems, including the small upper-left arrow and the two wings at the long shaft. Retain these literal paths instead of the former regularized cluster. The separate large loop has an inward stroke but no unambiguous letter or arrowhead; circlearrowleft versus G remains doubtful. Neighboring cap fragments and duplicate long shafts are excluded.

The outline is uneven and interrupted near the top. A small top point is separate from the larger interior point, and the short line leaving the interior point is solid. The descending connector starts on the heavy front arc and bends into the low loop. The numbered segment retains the filled 0 end, 1 label, and detached tick above its other end. The neighboring crossing curve is retained only in the full-sheet geometry.

The crop shows a small ring near the top, broken rear meridians, separate short arrowheads on the equator, hatching and partially retraced boundaries. Keep the first labels: the left lower closed oval is 0, the two joined loops are infinity, and the right upright with flag and foot is 1 rather than alpha. The oval above infinity contains a central mark and short upright, so 0 versus circled point remains doubtful. The extra filled point adjoining that oval is a distinct mark. Literal traces of those labels are replaced with their text once, without making extra unlabeled rings.

Three parallel strokes join the lower rings, with separate dark points at the rings and their contacts. The left lower appendages are short stems, and the right lower appendage contains two joined small loops. The outline and upper connection have visible gaps and partial retracing. Retain those paths and the small upper oval, while excluding the long crossing line and fragments of the adjacent cancelled note already transcribed elsewhere.

The small top oval has a separate short tick and an interrupted upward extension. The larger lower loop is partly retraced along its left and upper sides and ends in a long lower-right trailing curve. These literal contours are more faithful than a smooth closed loop with straight attachments; no alphabetic identity is assigned.

The two small circle outlines and several rings have open gaps, short crossing strokes and a leftward/downward boundary arrow. The separate narrow oval remains distinct. Adopt the literal traces, but omit two crossing full-sheet lines and the partial adjacent map and dome contours so that their ink is represented only once.

The large outer and inner ovals are uneven and open, the top rim has a doubled trace and an adjoining loop, and the lower small ring leads to two separate outgoing curves. The isolated narrow left oval is retained. The independent paths preserve these details more closely than the former regular ellipses and single spiral; neighboring upper and right context strokes are omitted.

The pole connection has two distinct contours, a small leftward arrow occurs below the rear dashed line, and a separate broken leftward arrow lies near the bottom. The rings are uneven or open, with filled marks at their contacts. Retain the thin outward upper-right ray and the explicit doubled edges, gaps and points; do not regularize their count or make the broken arrows continuous.

The black outline, two upper rings, rear broken arc, contact strokes, filled points and small crossing wiggle are visible. The main reader also confirmed three left-rim and four right-rim contact points. Retain the green trace parallel to the upper dark arc and the green right descending stripe, which the blind grayscale path text omitted. The independent black geometry is adopted with these color and point corrections, excluding the duplicated crossing line and neighboring small-circle fragment.

The rotated crop has a curved four-sided outline with four filled vertices, four separate outside strokes and a thin crossing interior curve. Adopt the less regular independent paths and restore their original orientation and placement. Both formulas agree in letters, subscripts and signs; they remain once in the margin text, without duplicate nodes in the drawing.

After the doubtful initial avec, the low u and n and the compact ens are visible, rather than une classe. The next line has on fait, and 3 times 2 equals 6 is clear. The favored cartes and elliptiques outlines survive but are crossed too heavily to assert every letter, so both doubts are reopened. The final pair has two stem-and-foot ones, not a secure 4. No separate comma after éléments is seen.

The opening words and the full parenthesis are supported by the wide crop. The total superposes a long dark 7 diagonal and top bar with the short upright and crossbar of 4; their order is not established. The word after it begins with a looped descending p and has o, an n-like join, tall crossed t and final s; ponts is favored, points remains possible, and cartes is excluded. The short following word remains on/ou/or. The type phrase is physically interlinear below trouver, but its exact linear attachment remains uncertain. No arithmetic expectation chooses the overwritten total.

The crop visibly superposes the long dark descending diagonal and top bar of 7 with the short upright, crossbar and diagonal of 4. Both components must be represented. Their intersections do not establish which was written last; 4-to-7 is favored from the dark long leg, with 7-to-4 explicitly retained. The arithmetic is not used to force a final 14.

The opening stroke descends below the line and returns into a loop, supporting p rather than c. It is followed by an o, n-like joined strokes, a tall crossed t and a terminal s hook. There is no securely placed i dot. Favor ponts with points as the surviving alternative; cartes no longer fits the initial letter.
